sources.entry: ccvitals by educlopez - The prettiest statusline for Claude Code — pure bash, never blocks your prompt. Usage quota, context window, git status & more.

summary.one_liner: ccvitals is a pure-bash, zero-Node statusline for Claude Code that shows session vitals such as usage quota, context window, cost, and git status in the terminal without blocking the prompt.
keywords: see how much context is left
summary.what_it_does: ccvitals renders a configurable one-line or two-line status display for Claude Code. Modules include directory, model, context-window bar, 5-hour and 7-day quota bars with reset timers, git branch and change counts, session cost and duration, token throughput, vim mode, active agents, pending tools, todo progress, and daily or 30-day spend. Modules are enabled through a JSON config file, and per-project .ccvitals.json files can override global settings. Quota data is read from Claude Code's stdin first and falls back to an OAuth API call, cached for 60 seconds with background refresh. Six built-in color themes and a custom hex palette are available, along with a powerline segment mode that requires a Nerd Font. An optional hook script records session titles and turn counts. Installation is via Claude Code plugin marketplace, Homebrew, or a git clone with a symlinked install script.
use_cases: see remaining 5-hour and weekly Claude quota in the terminal
show context window fill level while coding with Claude Code
track session and daily Claude Code spending
display git branch and changed files next to the Claude prompt
customize a status line layout and colors for Claude Code
monitor running tools, sub-agents, and todo progress during a session
notable: Never blocks the prompt: stale-while-revalidate cache with background refresh
Detects the 1M context tier so context percentage stays accurate past 200k
Pure bash plus jq with no Node runtime
Two-line layout and per-project config overrides
Opt-in modules such as spend history, tool and sub-agent tracking, and session titles via hooks
caveats: Powerline mode needs a Nerd Font, and responsive layout is skipped when powerline is on
Quota fallback reads OAuth credentials from the macOS Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json
Many modules are opt-in and the session module requires running the hooks installer
The historical spend module only accumulates data from the time the daily module was first enabled
